posts.content_html_raw:
I think it'd be a mistake to assume everything is happening sequentially as we're playing it. This game references reincarnation, multiple timelines, and there's clearly something going on behind the 4th wall as well. I think we're experiencing a narrative pieced together through multiple timelines and decisions by the main character.

It's not a complete theory of course but it would explain some things. Why Maya seems to know so much about us right off the bat (it's already been established that she can remember every cycle), why we know exactly what to say to Ami at her parents' grave without knowing how we know what to say, why we can date multiple girls who all live together at the same time without them seeming to realize.

I think we as the player experience scenes in sequence that actually occur in completely separate lifetimes.

It's a convoluted idea that's probably wrong but I think it's nifty.

Since everyone is offering their two cents on this weird stuff here's mine
I didn't think there was anything *actually* special about the "other half of town" other then being a normal, poorer district. HOWEVER, I think it was meant to be symbolic of the "other half of the mind", the dark, strange, parts that Sensei and others try to hide when they are surrounded by the comforts of their daily life.

Though now that I thinking on it perhaps the town's other half reminds Sensei of his old life before coming to this world, which is why he seems to hate being there so much and act so strange there.

As for the Ami scene when he was like "Who's words are these?" , I think that was the moment he *actually* wanted to be her kind, loving uncle as opposed the just taking advantage of his life for his own selfless gains, but this causes conflict within him because he *knows* that he isn't that Sensei so he feels like he's torn between those feelings, thus "Who's words are these?"(READ AS: These aren't my words, aren't feelings I should be feeling, but I want to and am)

thanks for the demos said:
Would we miss any actual content by increasing love increments to +5 per event, or simply setting everyone's love to 100?
Click to expand...
Don't think there's anything you'd miss off the top of my head. You could probably just console-command yourself to 100 with everyone and bypass the grind if it bothers you that much. I used the increments of five because I felt like it was a good amount of passed-time in order to get to the next part of each girl's story. I feel like the pacing would be off if their events just came one after another without anything between them, so that chill period was what I decided on and don't really intend to change. The grind will get easier as time goes by that with the addition of more calling/invite events (EX: You can now bring Ami up 3 points on weekends as you can spend each part of the day with her).

posts.content_html_raw:
(It's kind of a long one. Sorry!)
Just finished this game and I gotta say... Wow! That was awesome!

At first I wasn't really into it. But gradually I started to like it. The grind was kind of off-putting at first. But then I realised it wasn't actually that bad and the events were (mostly) worth it. It reminded me a little bit of Stardew Valley, actually. Where you grind for awesome events. The grind there is much, much worse tho, not even comparable.

My favourite event is definitely the one where you meet Chinami. Couple of reasons. First, she's awesome, and adorable af. Second,
when she shows you her mom's pic while saying she's never alone and Chika is crying. That was heartbreaking. Hit me right in the feels. I wish we could've huged Chika or something like that. I hope we can build Chika her castle. It doesn't seem this game is going to be the "wholesome harem' type, but still. I can dream.

<sidenote>
I don't what the developer's plans are in regards to Chinami, but I hope she doesn't become a romanceable character
</sidenote>

Secret events were really good, I liked them a lot. Some where kind of bothersome to trigger, particularly the last one. I hope in the future we get information to tie them all together. Maybe if
Maya wasn't such a bitch about it, we would know more by now. I guess there's a reason she's a heartless cunt. It's not like the MC is any better, but at least he's kinda friendly. I like that one of the main characters is involved in this side of the story. I enjoyed the hex text and the fucked up sprites and all of that. The 'rewrite' event was definitely a highlight of this side of the story. The swim trip event was also kind of funny, with Ayane standing on the wall and flying away (if I remember correctly). I'm waiting to see where all of this goes.

I liked a lot the amount of detail in scenes. The girls rooms, although they follow the same 'formula', you know, with the whiteboard and whatnot, were very nice to discover. The first time you visit each of them you kinda snoop around and they all have their own personality. One detail in particular I really enjoyed was in the bathhouse, when the girls are talking, you can see Ayane's gun together with their mobile phones. That was cool. There were other details like that one, but now I'm having trouble remembering them.

As for the girls, it feels like they were crafted so as to tick as many boxes as possible in terms of 'types'; not to miss any of the normal preferences. But still, in general, I liked everyone.

My favourite are definitely (alphabetical order) Chika, Rin and Sana. I enjoyed their events a lot, and saved those for last.
Chika's events were kind of wholesome, I loved them. The beach with Chinami and Yumi was nice. The one where Chinami is wearing that dog helmet was amazing aswell. The event(s) where Rin isn't sleeping were awesome. I liked those a lot. In particular, the event where you go into her room and she's just sitting there staring at the floor was my favourite of hers. I liked Rin in general; she's kinda weird, in a good way. Sana is just Sana. How could she not be among your top 3?

The ones I liked the least are Maya and Miku, but that's my fault. Maya I kind of elaborated in the 2nd spoiler. I wished she were more direct, but that ain't happening. Explanations coming somewhere in the future I hope. Still liked her overall role in the story, even though we don't know shit. As for Miku, just not my type. I'm not saying she's bad or anything, just not my type. I also feel she's kind of underdeveloped (not sure if this is the right word for this). Maybe she was pushed aside a little to let her teammates get some scenes? I don't know.

As for the other main girls (MC's students), I liked all of them, no complaints. The only thing I guess is that I just wished the MC wasn't such a dick sometimes.
I hated the event where he forces himself on Yumi. Also, I'm not a fan of some things he does/says around Makoto and Futaba.
But that's just me, I guess. I don't particularly enjoy then the main character is kind of a dick to others without reason.

Side girls were pretty good aswell. I enjoyed each and every one of them. I'm not sure if I liked Karin or Kaori the most. I know there's not much content with them, but I hope they get at least one new addition per update.

I liked that the girls are not a bunch of bimbos with huge tits and such. Their bodies are 'reasonable' (as reasonable as can be in a game lol). Don't get me wrong, I love big titties, but there's something about 'normal' girls that makes me appreciate the story a whole lot more.

Overall I really liked this one, definitely among my top 10, so far. I just hope it doesn't follow the path of so many others; they start out amazing and then take a nose dive. But it doesn't seem that will be the case. I feel like a lot of care went into it. I'll wait for the next update to confirm, but you might have gotten yourself a new patron. Cheers!

PS: Something that as kind of weird was that, when presented the options of what to do ('go somewhere' and 'call someone'), once you selected one of them there was no button to go back if you changed your mind? Is this on purpose? I'm not sure if anyone has pointed it out. I guess you could just rollback, but still.

The main saves folder is in appdata/roaming/renpy/Test2 (Confusing, I know. When I first made the game in RenPy I simply labeled it as Test 2 but by the time I realized that was what it named the saves folder, it was too late to change it without losing progress for thousands of people).

If saves don't transfer automatically for some reason, please refer to this guide that someone on the Discord typed up about transferring them:
HOW TO TRANSFER SAVES ON ANDROID: 1. Open up the new Ren'py port to create a file path. 2. Most phones should have a "files" app, if not, most free ones on the app store will work perfectly fine. From there, open up your internal storage, once it's open, click on the folder labeled "Android", then "data". 3. You're gonna see a ton of folders labeled "com.name", you're going to look for the one that's labeled as "ll_androidmo.me". Once you have found that folder, open it, click on "files" and now you should see a folder labeled "saves". That houses all your manual, and auto saves. Copy (or cut) the folder by holding down on it and selecting the option. 4. Go back to the "data" folder that has all the "com." folders, now locate the one labeled as "com.selebus.lil040". Go into the "files" folder and paste the save folder in. If it asks you to replace, that's perfectly fine. 5. Close out of the renpy port of LiL and reopen. 6. Once you verify your saves have been ported over, the old app can be deleted.

Go into the "files" folder and paste the save folder in. If it asks you to replace, that's perfectly fine. 5. Close out of the renpy port of LiL and reopen. 6. Once you verify your saves have been ported over, the old app can be deleted.

I don’t think willpower has anything to do with it. Horror is the most subjective genre out there. What terrifies one person might make someone else laugh. That’s the challenge in creating it and why the rise of horror in the 80s worked out so well.

That’s why I’ve always liked psychological horror. It’s one thing to show people creepy imagery but what I really want them to do is think. The most horrifying things for me have always been the things that I don’t understand. And even if there are people who aren’t getting scared by the horror elements, as long as they’re thinking about what’s going on or questioning the underlying meanings, I’ve succeeded in my book.

Really cool idea and I'm glad a lot of people seem to like it a lot. Judging from the cute little sprinkle of tags there I wasn't as sure the psycho scenes would be paced as they are. The scenes were pretty well done in their creepy little way, but I don't like the suspense of not knowing at all when shit hits the fan next.

When it is in progress of just blasting the room it's cool.

When I get wound up for a bit then the fan pops and gets me, I'm cool.

When I go 50 in game days knowing I only saw like two re-watchable scenes and I saw like 7 creep scenes it's not cool for me.

It's too off the beaten path for me and I feel like I am being punished too often for playing this like a standard VN but I also don't really have a choice. It doesn't really feel like I'm playing it so much as it's playing me and I have a life for that feeling.

If that's what you are going for, hell yeah you are doing a great job and it's great how it starts out inconsequentially, like any other amnesia scenario, but slowly begins to seep into everything but subtly.

If not, might I suggest some kind of visual tell? Like a filter of subtly lowered resolution or something when the next event is either coming or enough triggers has made the next event ready? It would make the suspense cycle more controllable as you condition your player to respond, sometimes unconsciously if you get the tell right, to a specific stimulus as opposed to turning people like me into nervous chihuahuas who just say fuck it and put the game down.

Either way good work. It's enjoyable. Not enough for me haha! But clearly there is a product of quality here.

That is intentional and has always been my writing style in this and other games. I understand that it’s not for everyone and I knew that coming into this, but it’s not really something I want to change. The sudden and random genre-shifts in places you wouldn’t expect give the game a unique feeling. I don’t want people to have hints of what could be coming next. I want it to be closer to how life is in general- a series of coincidences, with many of which being horrible or unexpected, but some of them just seemingly unimportant or strange.

The structure is a sort of testament to the game itself in a sense. Both are completely nonsensical and overly technical at times when they probably don’t need to be. Would it be easier to change that? Yeah. Would it make for a more comprehensible story? Probably, yeah. But that’s not what I want this narrative to be, and I think that will only become more apparent in the future.

I totally get it, though! That critique was something I knew I was going to hear when I released this. It’s just how I want it to be.
